theorem_title: Shao's Lemma 2.1: the symmetric averaging inequality
natural_language_statement:
Let $n$ be even with $n \ge 6$ and let $a_0 \ge a_1 \ge \dots \ge a_{n-1}$ be reals in $[0,1]$. Suppose that for every triple of indices $i, j, k$ with $i + j + k \ge n$ we have

$$a_i a_j + a_j a_k + a_k a_i \le \tfrac{5}{8}(a_i + a_j + a_k).$$

Then $\sum_i a_i \le \frac{5}{8} n$.

The proof uses this through its contrapositive: an average above $5/8$ yields one triple of indices summing to at least $n$ on which the inequality is strict the other way.

The hypothesis $n \ge 6$ is needed. Shao gives the counterexample $a = (1, 0.6, 0.5, 0.41)$ at $n = 4$.
source: Xuancheng Shao, "A density version of the Vinogradov three primes theorem", Duke Math. J. 163 (2014) 489-512, arXiv:1206.6139v2, https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.6139, Lemma 2.1
